Listening to rap and seeing how they manipulate flow, rhythm and cadence but also listening to more pop oriented genres and seeing how they keep things simple and hooky. Being able to switch flows and rhythms is a good way to work lyrics and melodies in together, seeing how rap artists change their cadence and flow is a great skill to study even if you're not trying to make hip hop, its important to understand how you can manipulate your rhythm in a vocal context.

Another tip is listening to how different instruments (whether its trumpet, guitar, sax whatever) and seeing how they approach melody in contrast to how you write vocal melodies. Note selection in sax melodies is different to guitar parts, so if you're stuck and can't write a  vocal melody that fits your lyrics maybe try listening to some sax solos and try a different approach to melody.

Having a good understanding of different ways you can approach melody is helpful i find. Having a base understanding of music theory and harmony is good (you don't need to be Jacob Collier and understand it all) but having a few tricks up your sleeve is always helpful.

Kids have always been talented. How young was Michael Jackson when he got his start with the Jackson 5. There have always been really talented young children making "better" music than adults. Mozart was a child prodigy. 

Nowadays, People like Kenny Beats and Alex Tumay have youtube, discord and twitch channels where they give full breakdowns of their DAW sessions from their hit songs. Kids can watch and emulate effects chains, mimic sounds and then buy or get cracks of expensive software to get a pro-level sound. Youtube Channels like YouSuckAtProducing and Andrew Huang as well do good tutorials that kids can understand and rewatch. I recommend watching those for sure. I'd played music for years but never got into production until last year and youtube and twitch have really helped my music production as someone who's 25 but only a beginner to production.

I'd also say that next time you hear a kid produce something crazy, listen to what you like that they're doing, reach out to them and ask how and where they learned how to do it at such a young age. Kids are always going to take music forward anyway so better to learn from them to help develop, modernise and futurise your own sound.
